# `prefer-array-list-last`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports `list.items[list.items.len - 1]` when `list` is proven to have a
standard array-list type.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

`last().?` names the operation directly and keeps the list expression in one
place.

## When it fires

The receiver must resolve to an explicitly typed `std.ArrayList` or
`std.ArrayListUnmanaged`. The rule does not add an emptiness check; it preserves
the original operation's requirement that the list be non-empty. The rewrite is
eligible for fix-all.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn last(list: std.ArrayList(u32)) u32 {
    return list.items[list.items.len - 1];
}

fn terminate(list: std.ArrayList(u32)) void {
    list.items[list.items.len - 1] = 0;
}
```
